reply_text:
I found one dated AI prediction from LeCun in 2023 that I could check against a page I opened. A second one is likely real, but I only saw it in search snippets.

- **The dated prediction (June 2023):** in a recorded interview with Rudyard Griffiths before the June 22 Munk Debate, LeCun said that "within five years" autoregressive LLMs will disappear and be replaced by more controllable systems. The words are in the transcript on thehub.ca.
- **The unconfirmed one:** several snippets have a talk version of the same claim: "five years from now nobody in their right mind would use them". Its date and venue are unknown. One snippet came from a LinkedIn post that blocked fetching, and another from a Medium post I never opened. So it isn't a candidate.
- **The 20VC podcast (page dated May 2023):** the uListen transcript says "within a few years, nobody in their right mind would use autoregressive LMs". "A few years" counts as undated, and it isn't about when AGI arrives, so it stays out.
- **One undated AGI remark (December 2023):** in the Wired interview with Steven Levy, LeCun said that how long it takes for machines to become smarter than humans "could be years, it could be centuries". I read this in a forum repost of the article, not on wired.com, because the fetch tool refused the Wired link.
- **The CNBC report on the December 2023 event for FAIR's 10th anniversary (Meta's AI research lab), with the "cat-level"/"dog-level" remarks:** I couldn't check it. I had used all 6 page openings, including one spent on the refused Wired link.
- **Already recorded:** I didn't come across the January 2023 "teenagers will train image models within two years" claim.

I ran 9 of the 12 searches, with the three fixed ones first.
